deltaScope: Read-only post-freeze review of the process-lock PID-reuse fix on the exact-head evidence export (compare recorded lock timestamp against the live Linux process start time via /proc with 120 s tolerance; route mismatches to the reviewed recovery path instead of a false live-owner error) plus the DeepSource JS-0246 template-literal follow-up. Two changed lines in one production file plus six new test assertions in one test file; every replacement was checked for behavior preservation with the targeted 6/6 process-lock suite on Linux and Windows plus the full local suites. No provider, account, deployment or live-order action was performed.

production.change: linuxProcessStartTimeMs reads /proc/<pid>/stat and /proc/stat btime to derive the live process start time; processIdentityMatches requires the lock timestamp within 120 s after process start, otherwise the stale lock resolves to RecoveryRequiredError exactly like an absent owner. Non-Linux platforms and unreadable /proc fall back to the previous kill(pid,0) behavior. Nothing is ever deleted automatically; fail-closed semantics are unchanged. The follow-up expresses the /proc/<pid>/stat path as a template literal (byte-identical).

runtimeBinding: executorTreeHash covers the exact exchange_executor Python inventory, which this delta does not touch. ccxt_implementation_reviews.py remains the separately trusted approval root.

results.pythonFullSuite: 587 passed (exchange_executor discover) plus 13 internal-TLS and 13 Hyperliquid-bound preflight tests passed
results.rootBuild: TypeScript, declaration copy and Vite production build passed

securityAssessment.conclusion: The delta closes the container-restart false-live-owner loop without disabling a rule, excluding a source file or weakening provider, filesystem, transport, mutation or secret boundaries. Fail-closed behavior is preserved and extended: PID reuse now resolves to explicit reviewed recovery.
securityAssessment.processLock: The /proc reads are read-only and Linux-gated with fallback; the 120 s tolerance only accepts locks plausibly written by the live process and never deletes state; malformed locks still fail closed.

limits: Author-reviewed delta (no separate subagent runtime was available in this environment); behavior preservation is additionally proven by the targeted 6/6 process-lock suite on Linux and Windows, the full local suites on the final SHA, and the green exact-head cloud CI jobs (Quality OS lint/tests/mutation/browser, SonarQube, Codacy, DeepSource).
Implementation evidence only; provider/account acceptance and live trading remain false.

Evidence ran on WSL Ubuntu with Node v22.22.1/npm 10.9.9 (same majors as CI) and a reused hash-pinned Python 3.12.14/CCXT 4.5.75 venv (coverage/ruff reinstalled with --require-hashes); one scratch symlink made the Debian node-adjacent npm CLI discoverable for the receipt-runner test.
